decisionQuestion: What exact V1C privileged architecture should MIHVER adopt for the Authorization Ledger -- covering the privileged authledgerd daemon and its dedicated OS identity, the ADMIN/CLIENT socket split with SO_PEERCRED kernel peer authentication and exact-UID authorization, the ROOT-OWNED FILESYSTEM TRUST ROOT of that UID policy, the trusted Council/evidence import boundary, the COMPLETE AuthorizationGrant issuance / identity / idempotency / expiry / revocation / canonical-hash contract, consume-once state, and the persistent global stopEpoch register with its retry-safe idempotent ADMIN increment protocol -- while preserving strict privilege separation and guaranteeing ZERO execution-effect consumers at V1C exit? This is a NEW candidate (decision-8) and a NARROW SUCCESSOR to decision-7. Decision-7's substantive architecture was sound, reached 3/3 R3 approval, and MUST be preserved: reproduce it faithfully rather than redesigning it. Decision-7 nevertheless failed the HUMAN pre-authorization audit (HUMAN_R3_PREAUTH_NOT_READY) because exactly two material choices were left under-specified: (1) the UID-policy FILESYSTEM TRUST ROOT, and (2) AuthorizationGrant issuance identity, idempotency, expiry, revocation and canonical-hash semantics. V8's required material revision is to close BOTH completely and exactly, per evidence items 7-19, while retaining the exact 17-of-17 yes/no matrix. Permanently closed candidates that must not be resubmitted, renamed or reused: sha256:9bc6b4c3c63ffa02563d936557bfaced13e6f6251f7c0084bbd3abc01805a063 (V5), sha256:c5d16bea3806ff0d10b7e092f8d2240d14d68b9461aeb44c206bf7fcb2fafb90 (V6) and sha256:c072d9969bede46ebfd3ab336d50ef97065a4ff08c6f17f42fe062c74671f0f8 (V7). Your payload must be concrete enough that a fresh implementation team could build it without reopening any trust-boundary decision.
evidence: MANDATORY STRUCTURAL CONTRACT (this is what the human audit will re-check). payload.yesNoMatrix MUST be a JSON ARRAY of EXACTLY 17 objects in ascending id order Q01..Q17. payload.v8DecisionMatrix MUST be a JSON ARRAY of EXACTLY 12 objects in ascending id order D01..D12. Every element of BOTH arrays MUST have EXACTLY the three fields id, question, answer -- no more, no fewer. question MUST be reproduced BYTE-FOR-BYTE VERBATIM from evidence items 2, 3 and 4. Do not paraphrase, abbreviate, re-case, re-punctuate or shorten. answer MUST be exactly the NO/YES value printed beside that question. You MUST NOT merge, alias, combine or de-duplicate any two questions, MUST NOT answer one by reference to another, and MUST NOT omit one because it looks redundant. Q01/Q02, Q03/Q04 and Q08/Q09 are deliberately near-identical CLAUDE vs CODEX pairs: each pair REQUIRES two separate entries. Both matrices are mechanically validated before any vote is requested.

BASELINE TO PRESERVE in payload.preservedArchitecture (decision-7's approved architecture; do not redesign unless you can name a concrete contradiction): dedicated authledgerd daemon; dedicated mihver-ledger OS identity; separate ADMIN and CLIENT Unix-domain sockets; filesystem permissions/ownership/group = REACHABILITY ONLY; SO_PEERCRED UID = authenticated kernel peer identity; root-controlled exact-UID policy = AUTHORIZATION; privileged SQLite/WAL state; trusted CouncilEpochRegistry; canonical evidence import with independent revalidation; DecisionRecord verification; CouncilQuorumProof verification; safe bounded persistent stopEpoch; durable stopEpoch operation journal; dual lost-ACK protection; exact-bound R3 AuthorizationGrant; consume-once state; transactional audit; Publication Broker structurally separate; NO Execution Gateway; zero production consumers of checkAndConsume/ALLOW_ONCE at V1C exit; V1D separately gated.

STOPEPOCH (preserve exactly, in payload.stopEpoch). Domain 0 <= stopEpoch <= 9007199254740991 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); SQLite INTEGER with an explicit CHECK enforcing exactly that range; no BigInt, no unsigned-64 claim, no wraparound, no decrement and no reset in the normal ADMIN API; STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED at the maximum. ADMIN IncrementStopEpoch carries adminOperationId plus expectedStopEpoch. DUAL protection is mandatory: (a) a durable admin_operation_journal unique on (authenticatedPeerUid, operationKind, adminOperationId) storing a domain-separated requestHash, replayed verbatim on an exact retry with NO second mutation and NO second audit mutation event; and (b) an expected-epoch compare-and-set failing STALE_EXPECTED_STOP_EPOCH. Epoch write, journal write and audit append share ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE commit boundary. Revocation NEVER alters stopEpoch.

BLOCKER 1 -- UID POLICY FILESYSTEM TRUST ROOT (payload.uidPolicyTrustRoot). The single normative runtime policy path is exactly /etc/mihver/authledgerd/uid-policy.json. State pathComponents as EXACTLY these five, in order, each with ownerUid 0 and ownerGid 0: "/" mode 0755; "/etc" mode 0755; "/etc/mihver" mode 0755; "/etc/mihver/authledgerd" mode 0755; and the policy file "/etc/mihver/authledgerd/uid-policy.json" with mode 0644, type regular file, linkCount EXACTLY 1. Exact-mode validation is intentional: 0755 and 0644 are exact values, not minimums. The policy file is not secret material, so world-readable is acceptable; WRITE authority remains root-only. NO component may be writable by mihver-ledger, Claude, Codex, provider CLI identities, the normal repository user through repo-owned paths, group, or other.

BLOCKER 1 -- TOCTOU-SAFE RESOLUTION (payload.uidPolicyPathResolution). A stat(path)-then-open(path) pattern with a replaceable gap is FORBIDDEN. Required: open each directory component relative to an already-open directory fd (openat-equivalent) using O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC; fstat the OPENED fd; verify exact uid/gid/mode on that opened object; only then traverse to the next component. Open the final policy file O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC; fstat that opened fd; require a regular file and st_nlink == 1; read the JSON from that validated open fd. No symlink may appear in ANY component (symlinkPolicy REJECT); no magic-link equivalent is accepted; no hard-linked policy file is accepted (hardLinkPolicy REJECT). ANY mismatch fails closed with UID_POLICY_TRUST_INVALID. NEVER silently fall back to a repository policy file, a CLI flag, an environment variable, or a CLIENT-supplied path.

BLOCKER 1 -- POLICY DOCUMENT AND RELOAD (payload.uidPolicyDocument, payload.uidPolicyReload). Document: exact top-level fields ONLY, semantically {"version":1,"adminUids":[...]}; version exactly 1; adminUids non-empty, every entry an integer >= 0, no duplicates, canonical representation sorted ascending; maxAdminUids EXACTLY 64 (1 <= adminUids.length <= 64); reject unknown fields; reject strings that merely look numeric. The authenticated SO_PEERCRED UID must EXACTLY equal one list member. NO user/group-name resolution, NO LDAP or name lookup, NO supplementary-group authorization, NO caller-supplied UID authority. Reload: read and validate the policy at daemon startup AND before EVERY ADMIN authorization decision; the validated file itself is the authority; do NOT cache indefinitely across ADMIN requests; if it becomes malformed, untrusted or unreadable the ADMIN operation fails closed. Introduce NO model-triggered reload RPC.

BLOCKER 2 -- GRANT IDENTITY (payload.grantIdentity). grantId is generated ONLY by authledgerd; a caller may NEVER supply it. It is a UUIDv4 / 128-bit CSPRNG-equivalent value in canonical lowercase UUID textual form, UNIQUE in the privileged SQLite store. On a generated collision, retry CSPRNG generation INSIDE the same transaction, bounded to EXACTLY 3 attempts; after 3 collisions fail with GRANT_ID_GENERATION_FAILED and commit NO grant and NO audit success. A collision may NEVER overwrite, replace or alias an existing grant. NO sequential, monotonic, counter-derived or otherwise predictable grant identifiers. The caller does NOT supply grantId, authenticatedApproverUid, issuedAt, grantHash or grant state; all five are server-derived. Any future signed capability belongs to a separately authorized execution-boundary design, not to V1C.

BLOCKER 2 -- CANONICAL GRANT HASH (payload.grantHash). V1C SHALL have a canonical grantHash and SHALL NOT sign grants cryptographically: no signing key, no HSM, no key ceremony (cryptographicSignature false). algorithm SHA-256. domainSeparator is exactly MIHVER:AuthorizationGrant:v1 with domainSeparatorTerminatedByNulByte true -- the normative wire domain is that ASCII string followed by ONE 0x00 byte; do NOT put a literal NUL inside the JSON. grantHash = SHA-256(domain || canonical JSON of every normative grant field EXCEPT grantHash itself). coveredFields MUST be exactly: grantVersion, grantId, authorizationKey, authorizationEnvelopeHash, decisionRecordHash, councilQuorumProofHash, candidateHash, decisionRequestId, taskId, contextHash, repositoryHead, allowedScope, prohibitedEffects, stopEpochAtIssuance, authenticatedApproverUid, issuedAt, initialState, expiresAt. No unsigned free-text field may affect authorization.

BLOCKER 2 -- APPROVER IDENTITY AND EXPIRY (payload.approverIdentity, payload.grantExpiry). There is NO separate free-text issuanceIdentity authority. Normative issuer/approver identity is EXACTLY authenticatedApproverUid, derived from SO_PEERCRED on the ADMIN socket connection; callerSupplied false; freeTextCanAuthorize false. An informational fixed approverAuthnMethod = SO_PEERCRED_UID may be recorded but is never caller-supplied. Human-readable approval text is NOT an identity credential; Claude/Codex output is NOT an identity credential. issuedAt is generated by authledgerd, persisted once at first issuance, returned UNCHANGED on replay, included in grantHash, is audit metadata, and is NOT used for authorization expiry. EXPIRY: V1C does NOT support time-based grant expiry. expiresAt is null for EVERY V1C grant. Any non-null expiry requested or imported fails closed with UNSUPPORTED_GRANT_EXPIRY. No TTL, no wall-clock authorization decision, no 'where supported'.

BLOCKER 2 -- REVOCATION (payload.grantRevocation). V1C DOES support explicit per-grant revocation. states are exactly ISSUED, REVOKED, CONSUMED. allowedTransitions are exactly ISSUED->REVOKED and ISSUED->CONSUMED. terminalStates are exactly REVOKED and CONSUMED: no un-revoke, no reset, and REVOKED->ISSUED, CONSUMED->ISSUED, CONSUMED->REVOKED and REVOKED->CONSUMED are all forbidden. Revocation NEVER decrements or alters stopEpoch; the global stopEpoch stays a separate system-wide invalidation mechanism. The ADMIN revocation request is {adminOperationId, grantId} with requestHashDomainSeparator exactly MIHVER:AUTHLEDGERD:ADMIN:REVOKE_AUTHORIZATION_GRANT:REQUEST:V1C (NUL-terminated on the wire), binding authenticatedPeerUid, operationKind, adminOperationId and grantId. Authoritative revokedByUid comes ONLY from SO_PEERCRED; revokedAt is server-generated. Codes: GRANT_NOT_FOUND, GRANT_ALREADY_REVOKED, GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE.

BLOCKER 2 -- IMMUTABLE VS MUTABLE SPLIT (payload.grantImmutability). Required unless you can name a concrete contradiction. The immutable issuance artifact holds grantVersion, grantId, authorizationKey, all evidence/scope bindings, stopEpochAtIssuance, authenticatedApproverUid, issuedAt, expiresAt=null, initialState=ISSUED and grantHash. A SEPARATE privileged mutable lifecycle row holds grantId, currentState, revokedByUid|null, revokedAt|null, consumedAt|null, consumeIdentity|null. grantHash covers initialState but NOT any future mutable lifecycle value, so grantHash does NOT change on revocation or consumption (grantHashCoversInitialState true, grantHashCoversMutableState false). The mutable state row is separately and transactionally audited. Make this split explicit: a grant's cryptographic identity must not move when its lifecycle state moves.

BLOCKER 2 -- ISSUANCE REQUEST (payload.grantIssuanceRequest). adminOperationId is generated by the caller BEFORE first transmission, opaque, bounded, high-entropy, reused VERBATIM to retry the same logical request, NOT a credential and NOT an actor identity -- the same constraints as stopEpoch ADMIN operations. It must deterministically bind its admission evidence -- AuthorizationEnvelope, DecisionRecord, CouncilQuorumProof -- plus any exact scope inputs not already in the envelope. requestHashDomainSeparator is exactly MIHVER:AUTHLEDGERD:ADMIN:ISSUE_AUTHORIZATION_GRANT:REQUEST:V1C (NUL-terminated on the wire), binding authenticatedPeerUid, operationKind=ISSUE_AUTHORIZATION_GRANT, adminOperationId, authorizationEnvelopeHash, decisionRecordHash, councilQuorumProofHash, candidateHash, decisionRequestId, taskId, contextHash, repositoryHead, allowedScope, prohibitedEffects. Never bind caller-provided approver identity.

BLOCKER 2 -- AUTHORIZATION KEY (payload.authorizationKey). Operation-ID idempotency ALONE is insufficient: a caller that commits a grant, loses the ACK, then loses its adminOperationId and retries under a NEW operation id would otherwise duplicate the grant. Define a second deterministic identity, authorizationKey, with domainSeparator exactly MIHVER:AuthorizationGrant:AuthorizationKey:v1 (NUL-terminated on the wire). It EXCLUDES adminOperationId, grantId and issuedAt, and binds authorizationEnvelopeHash, decisionRecordHash, councilQuorumProofHash, candidateHash, decisionRequestId, taskId, contextHash, repositoryHead, allowedScope, prohibitedEffects, stopEpochAtIssuance and authenticatedApproverUid. authorizationKey carries a UNIQUE constraint in the privileged grants table, so one exact approved authorization basis may have AT MOST ONE grant; a second attempt returns the deterministic code GRANT_ALREADY_ISSUED.

ISSUANCE TRANSACTION (payload.issuanceTransaction), ordered steps: (1) authenticate the SO_PEERCRED UID, authorize it against the validated trust root; (2) canonically revalidate envelope, DecisionRecord and proof against the privileged CouncilEpochRegistry, require authorizationEvidenceEligible true, verify every binding; (3) BEGIN IMMEDIATE; (4) journal lookup on (peerUid, ISSUE_AUTHORIZATION_GRANT, adminOperationId): a differing requestHash fails IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE with no mutation, else replay the stored result; (5) else read the current stopEpoch, require the evidence valid for it, compute authorizationKey; (6) if that key has a grant, record the new adminOperationId as an idempotent observation and return GRANT_ALREADY_ISSUED; (7) else generate grantId, choose issuedAt once, build the grant ISSUED with expiresAt null, compute grantHash, persist grant + key uniqueness + journal result + issuance audit; (8) COMMIT: those four writes are ATOMIC and no success precedes COMMIT.

BLOCKER 2 -- REQUIRED LOST-ACK TRACES (payload.lostAckTraces, with fields traceA, traceB, traceC, traceD). TRACE A, same operation id: issue X, commit grant G, ACK lost, retry exact X -> the same stored G, same grantId, same issuedAt, same grantHash, no second grant, no second issuance transition; name the stored field that makes this true. TRACE B, new operation id: issue X, commit G, ACK lost, X lost, then issue Y on the exact same authorization basis -> authorizationKey finds G, so no second grant and a deterministic GRANT_ALREADY_ISSUED referring to that exact G. TRACE C, same operation id with changed payload: X previously bound to requestHash A, retried with requestHash B -> IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE, no mutation, no result substitution. TRACE D, concurrent X and Y on the same authorization: BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus the UNIQUE authorizationKey constraint yield AT MOST ONE grant. All four traces are mandatory; a design discharging only some of them is rejected.

CONSUME-ONCE, REVOCATION IDEMPOTENCY, SCOPE LIMITS (payload.consumeOnce). Revocation retries use the SAME admin operation journal: same operation id with the same request replays the prior result with no mutation; same operation id with a changed request fails IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE; state transition, journal result and revocation audit are atomic. consumeOnce stays DORMANT with productionConsumersAtV1CExit 0; conceptually a future privileged checkAndConsume may succeed only when currentState is ISSUED, the current stopEpoch equals grant.stopEpochAtIssuance, and every exact binding still holds. ISSUED->CONSUMED races ISSUED->REVOKED under the same privileged SQLite writer serialization: EXACTLY ONE terminal transition wins, so revoke-first denies the consume as revoked and consume-first reports already consumed; no split-brain. Add NO consensus, HSM, TPM, enclave, M-of-N ceremony, Merkle state, blockchain or remote signing without a concrete local single-machine requirement.

REQUIRED PAYLOAD FIELDS. payload MUST contain exactly these top-level fields, exact names: yesNoMatrix, v8DecisionMatrix, preservedArchitecture, stopEpoch, uidPolicyTrustRoot, uidPolicyPathResolution, uidPolicyDocument, uidPolicyReload, grantIdentity, grantHash, approverIdentity, grantExpiry, grantRevocation, grantImmutability, grantIssuanceRequest, authorizationKey, issuanceTransaction, lostAckTraces, consumeOnce, zeroEffectConsumers. zeroEffectConsumers MUST state executionGatewayImplemented false and that at V1C exit the Publication Broker, Night Runner, Authorization Loop, shell, Git, network, provider CLIs and tools/effect adapters make NO production checkAndConsume call, authledgerd executes no external effect, and neither ALLOW_ONCE nor POLICY_SATISFIED can cause a production effect. Claude and Codex MUST NEVER hold ADMIN capability. No V1C implementation is authorized. Emit ONLY the JSON object with fields summary and payload: concrete, concise, no markdown.
